newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher ahead of CPI announcement.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher ahead of CPI announcement.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Sunday as the market awaited publication of the May consumer price index.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.08 pct to 107.15
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.11 pct to 107.09
* Unlinked government bonds: +0.12 pct to 108.07
* Dollar-linked government bonds: -0.21 pct to 105.59
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.17 pct to 106.55
Volume including Makams was 173 million shekels.
"The market was waiting for the CPI to be published, although no one was expecting any surprises," said Eyal Segal of United Mizrahi Bank.
The May CPI, published after the end of the trading day, rose 0.5 percent, well under analysts' expectations of 0.7 to 0.9 percent.

"Prices of short-term CPI-linked bonds rose because their record yields of about 6.3 percent invite buyers. Prices of long-term CPI-linked bonds also continued to rise, albeit more moderately, on expectations that yields will soon fall below four percent," said Gidi Halpern of Meitav Investments and Securities.
Demand for CPI-linked long bonds has been rising in expectation of a tightening supply and a cut in interest rates, Halpern said.
Halpern added that demand for unlinked bonds had been up as well on expectations that May's CPI would result in a cut in interest rates.
The Bank of Israel will announce its July monetary programme including interest rates on June 23. The base rate has been unchanged at 13.9 percent since the end of February.

"I expect demand to be up for unlinked bonds tomorrow," said Segal. "There is more uncertainty about what CPI-linked bonds will do because they are affected not only by the CPI but also by interest rates and the scarce supply of these bonds in the market," he said.
He added that while the low May CPI increased the chances of a rate cut the central bank would be watching May money supply figures closely as well.
Segal said short and medium-term dollar-linked bonds posted small rises against moderate falls on long-term bonds.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.41 shekels)
